sentences.text: For Respondent(s) : Mr. B.N.Sandu, PP with Mr. Pankaj Sisodia.
_____________________________________________________ HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE Order 19/07/2017 (1) Heard learned Counsel for the parties.

(2) Charged for having committed an offence punishable under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, the petitioner has been sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of six months and pay fine in sum of  1000/-.
The conviction and sentence dated 19.12.2001 has been affirmed vide decision dated 03.04.2002 by the learned appellate Court.
The adulterated sample was ice-candy.
The same was lifted on May 23, 1996.
(3) Having perused the testimony of the witnesses, learned Counsel concedes that the verdict of guilt cannot be faulted with but Counsel prays for directions to be issued as were made by the (2 of 3)

[CRLR-347/2002] Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported as 1997 (9) SCC 101,
N.Sukumaran Nair V/s Food Inspector.
In the said decision noting Section 433 of the Cr.P.C. the Court commute sentence of six months imprisonment directing fine to be deposited.
A latter judgment of the Supreme Court reported as 2004(5) SCC 721, Dayal Singh V/s State of Rajasthan differed from the law laid down in N.Sukumaran Nair's case.

entities.text: 2004(5) SCC 721, Dayal Singh V/s State of Rajasthan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In a third decision reported as 2009(12) SCC 646, State of Rajasthan V/s Jagdish Prasad noting that the offence of adulteration though took place nearly three decades back, the Court directed that the sentence would remain suspended to enable the petitioner therein to file an application before the appropriate Government to exercise power under Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

entities.text: State of Rajasthan V/s Jagdish Prasad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appropriate Government was directed to decide the representation.
(4) In a judgment delivered on July 10, 2017 in S.B.Criminal Revision No.404/1995, Shayam Sunder Vs. State of Raj.

entities.text: S.B.Criminal Revision No.404/1995, Shayam Sunder Vs. State of Raj
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I had an occasion to note aforesaid three decisions of the Supreme Court and had passed directions as were issued by the Supreme Court in Jagdish Prasad (supra) case.

(5) Dismissing the instant revision petition, I Saleem Khan vs State on 19 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117000143/
1 suspend the sentence imposed upon the petitioner for a period of four months directing that if the petitioner makes a representation to the appropriate Government for commutation of the sentence of imprisonment within two months, the same shall be considered by the appropriate Government and decision would be taken within two months.

entities.text: I Saleem Khan vs State on 19 July, 2017 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner need not surrender for a period of four months.

If the appropriate Government commutes the (3 of 3) [CRLR-347/2002] sentence, the petitioner need not surrender at all and in said eventuality the bail bonds and surety bonds furnished by the petitioner shall stand discharged.
